doc.title: Joe Wilder — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Teaching a few students
summary: He gave up teaching because of unpredictable studio calls.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: Becoming a teacher: jazz in schools and conservatories

blocks.x: Did you ever teach? Was that something you did?

Some years ago I did. I taught a couple kids. At that time I was very busy. So when you’d have a lesson scheduled for today at two o’clock, and the night before, I would get a call at eleven o’clock at night, a jingle date or something at two, I’d have to call and say, “You can’t come today.” So I just gave it up.
Did you enjoy it though? I can imagine you would have been wonderful.

Yeah, I liked it. Especially if you had a couple of kids who were interested. But even so, I’d have a kid come for an hour. I would be explaining something to him. I didn’t think he played it well enough. I’d just assume I hadn’t explained it to him

properly or he doesn’t understand. Sometimes you’d go an hour, two hours – hour-and-a­ half or two hours, because I felt it was my responsibility to make sure that he understood before he left. I usually got a pretty good response from the kids.
